gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Quantum draws every line with one unbroken stroke weight, loose and spaced out, best blown up for a word or two. Noto Sans Tangsa is the sans-serif partner, with wide, inviting round letters and short ascender stems.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Spaced-out and techy, Quantum keeps its mouths open and its ascenders short. Noto Sans Thaana has wide channels into each counter, so paragraphs of it should slide by without snagging.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-thai: Quantum has a single-weight outline look, spaced loosely with its mouths left open. Noto Sans Thai fills its lowercase like inflated glass beads, which should make extended reading feel soft and unhurried.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-vai: Noto Sans Vai sets words as solid blocks rather than skylines, with generous space between curve ends and stems. And Quantum, crossbars matching its stems, sets the techy tone that the blocky body text then settles.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Quantum reads like following a single thread, loose and spaced out. Noto Sans Wancho counters with a hulking lowercase like pressed chalk and an e with a wide gap at its terminal.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-yi: Noto Sans Yi gives Quantum a deep-bodied partner, its rounds left unsealed like an unlatched hook. Nudge the body size up a notch and those openings really show.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-pathway-extreme: Quantum lays its letters out like spaghetti, loose and spaced, and it looks best big and short. Pathway Extreme sets stubby ascenders and descenders beside a big x-height, with clear round openings.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-questrial: Clean tech lettering, spaced out with mouths open. Questrial follows with stencil-cut strokes of single weight and short stalks, so next to Quantum it feels steady and modern.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-radio-canada: Radio Canada gives c, s and z a full stance and a steady line, every curve left open. Let the body size grow a little beside Quantum's loose heading.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big has a monoline skeleton and an x-height that fills the line, with terminals ending well away from the stem. Quantum gives the spaced-out display flair; the body gives steady reading.
